question: Does the current canonical Universal adapter's deterministic no-photo fallback make blocked human_story@3 packet 005 safe and truthful to activate?

inputs.media_prerequisite_at_start: one authorized source-metadata-bearing real candid photo

automated_findings.brand_failure: The dark Natal wordmark is rendered on a dark travertine field without its light logo surface.

manual_findings: At 1080 pixels the fallback is a sparse typography poster, not the required candid work scene: there is no person, work environment, observable closing moment, or other primary subject.
The headline has a strong editorial silhouette and the text blocks remain unclipped, but the texture does not complete or demonstrate the supplied post-visit mechanism.
At 360 pixels the headline and CTA remain clear while the supporting line, offer, and wordmark recede sharply.
At 120 pixels the headline and CTA are the only reliable signals; the mechanism, offer, and brand attribution no longer carry the one-glance message.
Geometry success is therefore insufficient: the fallback is render-safe but semantically incompatible with human_story@3 and fails the shared brand-prominence floor.

decision.conclusion: A renderer-level deterministic fallback does not override the generator template, owner task, or media policy. Candidate E still requires authorized real candid photography.
decision.reusable_rule: Treat media fallbacks as candidate-valid only when the supplied strategy and task explicitly authorize the resulting visual class, the resolved CandidateV2 and alt text describe those exact pixels, and brand/message hard gates pass.

future_option: If a later experiment explicitly requests a typography-led non-human poster, reserve a new identity under a matching non-photo strategy and preserve a light logo surface; do not relabel this fallback as human_story or Candidate E.
limits: This diagnostic bypassed CandidateV2 generation and contains no server element UUIDs.
It does not score or compare advertising effectiveness and cannot establish an outcome winner.
It did not invoke a provider, image model, critic, publisher, campaign, or external channel.
